ei.subject: 영어1
ei.title: Life Is a Journey to Be Experienced

fullPassage:
Hi, everyone. My name is Minji Song, and I am the editor of an online teen magazine, Teens Today. I am honored to have been asked to give a talk. Many of our high school student subscribers send me messages with concerns about their future. So today, I will talk about the value of experiences in making a better future. For this talk, I asked my old friends to write down stories about what they experienced when they were younger. I would like to start by reading them one by one.

I was fond of swimming
One summer day, I was watching an Olympic swimming event on TV. The gold medalist looked fantastic, and I wanted to be just like him. I asked my parents if I could learn to swim. They approved and said, "Yes." Swimming was difficult at first, but after a year, I became a good swimmer. I felt tired but happy when I was out of breath after every practice. As I practiced more, my times got better and better. One day, my coach suggested that I enter a competition. He also advised me that for good results I should build muscle strength through weight training. The training was demanding, leaving me exhausted at times. Whenever I felt this way, I told myself, "No pain, no gain."

I performed in a play
I used to be quiet and shy when I was a child. My homeroom teacher told me one day that she was putting on a play for our school festival. She suggested that I take on a small role, saying that being in a play would be a good experience. So, I decided to do it. I was so nervous at the first rehearsal that I could not say my lines at all. However, as I practiced my lines more, I became more and more confident. On the day of the performance, I got anxious and my mind went blank just before I stepped on the stage. My classmates tapped me on the shoulder and encouraged me. Thanks to this, I was able to perform my lines perfectly.

I wanted to be a landscape architect
One day, I saw a poster advertising the city's landscape design contest. The instant I saw it, I got interested. After doing some research on the Internet, I discovered that landscape designing involves arranging and decorating outdoor spaces. I thought a landscape architect's work was impressive because the arrangement of plants and structures can transform a space. This inspired me to think about becoming a landscape architect. I found out that I had to be good at math and science in order to become a landscape architect. This is because landscape architects must calculate the dimensions and slopes of land as well as thoroughly examine environmental factors such as soil, air, and climate. I was not good at either subject at the time, so I decided to put more effort into studying them.

I was passionate about writing
When I was fourteen, I was hospitalized for several weeks. One day, I saw a piece of paper on the table. I was bored, so I picked it up and began writing things down to pass the time. I felt a sense of relief when I wrote what I wanted to do after leaving the hospital. That evening, I asked my mother to buy me a notebook. As I filled page after page, I realized that writing was more than just a way to kill time. As the years passed, my passion for writing grew stronger. So I started writing short stories and sharing them with my friends and family. I felt a sense of accomplishment whenever they told me my stories were good.

Can you guess what my friends do now? Are they a swimmer? An actor? A landscape architect? A novelist? Actually, all four of these people are me! I currently work as a magazine editor. As you can see, my preferences have changed over the years as I was exposed to new experiences. Every time my interest changed, I was worried about what I was going to become in the future. Do you also have similar concerns?

Changes in your interests and preferences are completely natural. Try to accept this process and keep an open mind. Exploring new things can sometimes lead to valuable experiences which will help shape your future. I myself tried many different things before I finally became an editor because I enjoyed writing. Thanks to these many interests, I can write articles about math and science, speak confidently in front of an audience, and relieve my stress by swimming.

Allowing yourself the opportunity to experience a variety of things is not a waste of time. Your school days are a time of self-discovery and personal growth. As you spend each day wisely, you will be able to figure out what kind of person you are and what you enjoy doing. Do not attempt to define yourself in just one way as you undergo this process. Be flexible. Remember that your potential is limitless.

Thank you for your time.

questions.passage: Hi, everyone. My name is Minji Song, and I am the editor of an online teen magazine. I am honored to ①<u>have been asked</u> to give a talk. Many of our high school student subscribers ②<u>send</u> me messages with concerns about their future. So today, I will talk about the value of experiences in ③<u>make</u> a better future. For this talk, I asked my old friends ④<u>to write</u> down stories about what they experienced.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ③make → making: 전치사 in 뒤에는 동명사(-ing)가 와야 한다.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ make → making: 'in making a better future' — 전치사 in 뒤에 동명사.
❌ ① have been asked: 'honored to have been asked' — 완료부정사 수동태. 강연 요청이 영광보다 먼저이므로 적절.
❌ ② send: 현재 습관적 행동. 복수주어(subscribers)+send 적절.
❌ ④ to write: 'asked + O + to V' 5형식 적절.
det.tip: 전치사 + V-ing(동명사): in making, by swimming, for writing 등. 전치사 뒤에 동사원형 불가.

questions.passage: One summer day, I was watching an Olympic swimming event on TV. The gold medalist looked ①<u>fantastic</u>, and I wanted to be just like him. I asked my parents if I could learn to swim. They approved and said, "Yes." Swimming ②<u>was</u> difficult at first, but after a year, I became a good swimmer. One day, my coach suggested that I ③<u>entered</u> a competition. He also advised me that for good results I should build muscle strength ④<u>through</u> weight training.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ③entered → enter: 'suggest that + S + (should) + 동사원형' 구문에서 동사원형이 필요하다.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ entered → enter: suggest that 절에서는 should가 생략된 동사원형 사용.
❌ ① fantastic: 2형식 동사 looked의 보어로 형용사 적절.
❌ ② was: 동명사 주어 Swimming은 단수 취급. was 적절.
❌ ④ through: '~을 통해'라는 전치사 적절.
det.tip: suggest/recommend/insist + that + S + (should) + 동사원형. 당위·요구·제안의 that절에서 should 생략 시 동사원형.

questions.passage: Exploring new things can sometimes lead to valuable experiences ①<u>which</u> will help shape your future. I myself tried many different things before I finally became an editor because I enjoyed ②<u>writing</u>. Allowing yourself the opportunity to experience a variety of things ③<u>are</u> not a waste of time. Do not attempt to define yourself in just one way as you ④<u>undergo</u> this process.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ③are → is: 동명사구 'Allowing yourself the opportunity...'가 주어이므로 단수 동사 is가 필요하다.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ are → is: 동명사 주어는 단수 취급. 'Allowing yourself... is not a waste.'
❌ ① which: 관계대명사 주격. 선행사 experiences를 수식.
❌ ② writing: enjoy + V-ing 적절.
❌ ④ undergo: 타동사로 this process를 목적어로 취함. 적절.
det.tip: 동명사 주어 = 단수 취급 → 단수 동사. 'V-ing ... is/was...' 구조.

questions.passage: One day, I saw a poster advertising the city's landscape design contest. The instant I saw it, I got ①<u>interested</u>. After doing some research on the Internet, I discovered that landscape designing involves arranging and decorating outdoor spaces. I thought a landscape architect's work was ②<u>impressive</u> because the arrangement of plants and structures can ③<u>transform</u> a space. This ④<u>discouraged</u> me to think about becoming a landscape architect.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 단어 중, 문맥상 의미가 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ④discouraged → inspired: 인상적이라고 생각한 후 조경 건축가를 꿈꾸게 되었으므로 '영감을 주었다(inspired)'가 맞다.
det.analysis:
✅ ④ discouraged → inspired: 인상적인 일을 보고 꿈을 꾸게 된 것이므로 '낙담시키다'가 아니라 '영감을 주다'.
❌ ① interested(관심이 생긴): 포스터를 보고 관심을 가졌으므로 적절.
❌ ② impressive(인상적인): 공간 변화 능력에 감탄했으므로 적절.
❌ ③ transform(변화시키다): 식물과 구조물로 공간을 바꿀 수 있다는 맥락 적절.
det.tip: inspired(영감을 주다) ↔ discouraged(낙담시키다). 'This inspired me to think about'은 원인→결과 구문.

questions.passage: As you can see, my preferences have changed over the years as I was exposed to new experiences. Every time my interest changed, I was worried about what I was going to become in the future. Changes in your interests and preferences are completely ①<u>natural</u>. Try to accept this process and keep an ②<u>open</u> mind. Exploring new things can sometimes lead to ③<u>valuable</u> experiences which will help shape your future. Allowing yourself the opportunity to experience a variety of things is not a ④<u>benefit</u> of time.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 단어 중, 문맥상 의미가 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ④benefit → waste: '다양한 것을 경험하는 것은 시간 낭비(waste)가 아니다'가 원문. 'benefit of time'은 영어에서 사용하지 않는 표현.
det.analysis:
✅ ④ benefit → waste: 'not a waste of time(시간 낭비가 아니다)'가 원문. 'not a benefit of time'은 문맥 반전.
❌ ① natural(자연스러운): 관심사 변화가 자연스럽다는 맥락 적절.
❌ ② open(열린): 열린 마음을 가지라는 조언 적절.
❌ ③ valuable(귀중한): 미래 형성에 도움 되는 경험이므로 적절.
det.tip: waste of time(시간 낭비) vs benefit(이득). 원문의 이중 부정 'is not a waste'에 주의.

questions.passage: I used to be quiet and shy when I was a child. My homeroom teacher told me one day that she was putting on a play for our school festival. She suggested that I take on a small role, saying that being in a play would be a good experience. So, I decided to do it. I was so nervous at the first rehearsal that I could not say my lines at all. However, as I practiced my lines more, I became more and more __________.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 처음에 긴장해서 대사를 못했지만, 연습할수록 점점 자신감(confident)이 생겼다.
det.analysis:
✅ ② confident: However로 전환. nervous→confident 반전.
❌ ① suspicious(의심하는): 연극 연습과 무관.
❌ ③ indifferent(무관심한): 연습을 계속했으므로 부적절.
❌ ④ frustrated(좌절한): 연습 효과가 긍정적이므로 부적절.
det.tip: However + 반전: 긴장→자신감. 'more and more + 비교급/형용사' = 점점 더.

questions.passage: Changes in your interests and preferences are completely natural. Try to accept this process and keep an open mind. I myself tried many different things before I finally became an editor because I enjoyed writing. Thanks to these many interests, I can write articles about math and science, speak confidently in front of an audience, and relieve my stress by swimming. Allowing yourself the opportunity to experience a variety of things is not a __________ of time.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 다양한 것을 경험하는 것은 시간 낭비(waste)가 아니다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① waste: 'a waste of time(시간 낭비)' 관용표현. 다양한 경험이 편집자가 되는 데 도움이 되었다는 맥락.
❌ ② period(기간): 'a period of time'은 기간이라는 뜻. '기간이 아니다'는 문맥 부적절.
❌ ③ matter(문제): 'a matter of time'은 시간문제. 문맥 불일치.
❌ ④ source(원천): 'a source of time'은 사용하지 않는 표현.
det.tip: a waste of time = 시간 낭비. waste(n. 낭비) = '허비, 쓸데없는 사용'.

questions.passage: One summer day, I was watching an Olympic swimming event on TV. The gold medalist looked fantastic, and I wanted to be just like him. I asked my parents if I could learn to swim. They approved and said, "Yes." Swimming was difficult at first, but after a year, I became a good swimmer. I felt tired but happy when I was out of breath after every practice. As I practiced more, my times got better and better.
questions.stem: 위 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?

det.korean: 연습을 더 할수록 시간(기록)이 더 나아졌다.
det.analysis:
✅ ④ 원문: 'As I practiced more, my times got better and better.'
❌ ① 금메달을 딴 것은 TV에서 본 선수이지 화자가 아님.
❌ ② 부모님이 허락(approved)했음.
❌ ③ 'difficult at first'이므로 처음에는 어려웠음.
det.tip: 세부 내용 변조 주의: '금메달리스트를 본 것' ≠ '금메달을 딴 것'.

questions.passage: When I was fourteen, I was hospitalized for several weeks. One day, I saw a piece of paper on the table. I was bored, so I picked it up and began writing things down to pass the time. I felt a sense of relief when I wrote what I wanted to do after leaving the hospital. That evening, I asked my mother to buy me a notebook. As I filled page after page, I realized that writing was more than just a way to kill time.
questions.stem: 위 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?
ch: 화자는 처음에 지루함을 달래기 위해 글을 쓰기 시작했다.
화자는 처음부터 글쓰기가 단순한 시간 때우기 이상이라고 생각했다.

det.korean: 지루해서(bored) 시간을 때우기 위해(pass the time) 글쓰기를 시작했다.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ 원문: 'I was bored, so I picked it up and began writing things down to pass the time.'
❌ ① fourteen(열네 살)이지 열다섯이 아님.
❌ ② 어머니에게 노트를 사달라고 했지 친구가 선물한 것이 아님.
❌ ④ 'realized that writing was more than...' — 나중에 깨달은 것이지 처음부터 아님.
det.tip: 숫자 변조(14→15), 인물 변조(어머니→친구), 시점 변조(나중에→처음부터)에 주의.

questions.passage: This is because landscape architects must calculate the dimensions and slopes of land as well as thoroughly examine environmental factors such as soil, air, and climate. I was not good at either subject at the time, so I decided to put more effort into studying them.
questions.stem: 위 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
ch: 조경 건축가는 땅의 넓이와 기울기를 계산해야 한다.
화자는 당시 과학은 잘했지만 수학은 못했다.
조경 건축가는 환경 요소를 철저히 조사해야 한다.

det.korean: ② '과학은 잘했지만 수학은 못했다' → 원문: 'not good at either subject' = 둘 다 못했다.
det.analysis:
✅ ② 불일치: 'either subject'는 수학, 과학 둘 다를 가리킴. 둘 다 못했다.
❌ ① 일치: 'calculate the dimensions and slopes of land.'
❌ ③ 일치: 'thoroughly examine environmental factors.'
❌ ④ 일치: 'decided to put more effort into studying them.'
det.tip: either 부정: 'not ~ either' = 둘 다 ~아니다. 'not good at either subject' = 두 과목 모두 못한다.

questions.passage: Changes in your interests and preferences are completely natural. Try to accept this process and keep an open mind. Exploring new things can sometimes lead to valuable experiences which will help shape your future. I myself tried many different things before I finally became an editor because I enjoyed writing. Thanks to these many interests, I can write articles about math and science, speak confidently in front of an audience, and relieve my stress by swimming.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
ch: 편집자가 되기 위해 글쓰기를 연습해야 한다는 것
스트레스 해소를 위해 운동이 중요하다는 것
다양한 경험이 미래를 만드는 데 도움이 된다는 것
수학과 과학 성적이 진로에 결정적이라는 것

det.korean: 다양한 경험이 귀중하며 미래를 만드는 데 도움이 된다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① 핵심: 'lead to valuable experiences which will help shape your future'.
❌ ② 글쓰기 연습이 아니라 다양한 경험 전체에 대한 이야기.
❌ ③ 운동은 한 가지 예시일 뿐 주제가 아님.
❌ ④ 수학/과학은 본문의 한 사례이지 주제가 아님.
det.tip: 주제 파악: 반복되는 키워드 'experiences', 'interests', 'different things' → 다양한 경험의 가치.

questions.passage: Allowing yourself the opportunity to experience a variety of things is not a waste of time. Your school days are a time of self-discovery and personal growth. As you spend each day wisely, you will be able to figure out what kind of person you are and what you enjoy doing. Do not attempt to define yourself in just one way as you undergo this process. Be flexible. Remember that your potential is limitless.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
ch: How to Get Better Grades at School
The Danger of Trying Too Many Things
Why You Should Focus on One Goal

det.korean: 변화를 받아들이고 자기 자신을 발견하라.
det.analysis:
✅ ④ Embrace Change and Discover Yourself: 글의 핵심 메시지. 유연함, 잠재력, 자기 발견.
❌ ① 성적 향상에 대한 내용 없음.
❌ ② 글의 입장은 '시간 낭비가 아니다'이므로 '위험'과 반대.
❌ ③ '한 가지에 집중'은 'Do not define yourself in just one way'와 정반대.
det.tip: 제목: 글 전체의 핵심 메시지를 압축. 'Be flexible' + 'self-discovery' + 'potential is limitless'.

questions.passage: The training was demanding, leaving me exhausted at times. Whenever I felt this way, I told myself, "<u>No pain, no gain.</u>" One day, my coach suggested that I enter a competition. He also advised me that for good results I should build muscle strength through weight training.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 "No pain, no gain."이 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
ch: 고통 없이는 성과를 얻을 수 없다.
아픔 없이는 병원에 갈 수 없다.
경쟁에서 이기려면 다른 사람을 이겨야 한다.

det.korean: "고생 없이는 얻는 것이 없다." 힘든 훈련을 견디면 좋은 결과를 얻을 수 있다는 의미.
det.analysis:
✅ ② 고통(pain) 없이는 성과(gain)를 얻을 수 없다. 힘든 훈련의 가치를 스스로에게 상기시키는 말.
❌ ① pain을 문자 그대로 '아픔/병'으로 해석. 비유적 표현.
❌ ③ 고통이 영원히 지속된다는 의미가 아님.
❌ ④ 경쟁이나 승리에 대한 내용이 아님.
det.tip: No pain, no gain. = 고생 없이 얻는 것 없다. 속담/격언. 운동, 학습 등에서 노력의 가치를 강조.

questions.passage: Can you guess what my friends do now? Are they a swimmer? An actor? A landscape architect? A novelist? Actually, all four of <u>these people</u> are me! I currently work as a magazine editor. As you can see, my preferences have changed over the years as I was exposed to new experiences.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 these people이 가리키는 것으로 가장 적절한 것은?
ch: 수영선수, 배우, 조경건축가, 소설가라는 화자의 과거 관심사들

det.korean: these people = 수영선수, 배우, 조경건축가, 소설가 = 모두 화자 자신의 과거 관심사를 반영한 가상의 인물들.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ 'all four of these people are me!' — 네 명 모두 화자 자신. 각각의 관심사를 '친구'로 표현한 것.
❌ ① 실제 친구가 아니라 화자 자신의 과거 모습.
❌ ② 청중은 언급되지 않음.
❌ ④ 구독자와 무관.
det.tip: 이 글의 반전: '네 친구'라고 소개했지만 실제로는 모두 화자 본인. 다양한 경험의 사례.

questions.passage: I was bored, so I picked it up and began writing things down to pass the time. I felt a sense of relief when I wrote what I wanted to do after leaving the hospital. As the years passed, my passion for writing grew stronger. So I started writing short stories and sharing <u>them</u> with my friends and family.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 them이 가리키는 것으로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: them = 단편 소설들(short stories). 'writing short stories and sharing them'에서 them은 short stories를 가리킨다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① 'I started writing short stories and sharing them' — them = short stories.
❌ ② friends and family는 'with' 뒤에 이미 명시됨. sharing의 대상(목적어)이 아님.
❌ ③ 메모는 앞선 문장의 내용. 'short stories'로 발전한 후의 이야기.
❌ ④ 노트는 한 권(a notebook).
det.tip: 대명사 them의 선행사: 가장 가까운 복수 명사 'short stories'. sharing A with B = A를 B와 나누다.

det.analysis: tapped와 and로 병렬 연결. 과거시제 tapped에 맞춰 encourage → encouraged.

accept: I felt a sense of accomplishment whenever they told me my stories were good

I felt a sense of accomplishment whenever they told me my stories were good.

det.korean: 그들이 내 이야기가 훌륭하다고 말할 때마다 성취감을 느꼈다.
det.analysis:
I felt a sense of accomplishment whenever they told me my stories were good.
구조: S + V(felt) + O(a sense of accomplishment) + 부사절(whenever they told me my stories were good).
det.tip: a sense of accomplishment = 성취감. whenever = ~할 때마다. 'told me (that) my stories were good' 간접화법.
